pages.title: Dyson Array
pages.text: Surrounds a captive star with a swarm, and eventually a sphere, of collectors.$(br2)Generates power.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.

Freeman Dyson, 1960: a civilisation hungry enough for energy would wrap its star in collectors, and we could spot it by its waste heat. I appear to be that civilisation now.$(br2)This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

Loading it: a $(item)Stellar Core$() in the first slot. $(item)Dyson Swarm Satellites$() (up to 500) in the second - or leave a $(item)Von Neumann Probe$() there and it builds the swarm by itself. $(item)Dyson Shell Segments$() in the third: 64 close the sphere, but you need 100 satellites before shells can be mounted.

The yield, as I have worked it out:$(br2)Output = base x satellites/50 x (1 + shells/16)$(br2)and doubled again once the sphere is complete. A finished sphere is the brightest thing I have built, and from outside you cannot see it at all.

pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

One of millions. Feed them to a Dyson Array.$(br2)Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().
Builds copies of itself from whatever it finds. Put one in a Dyson Array.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$().
A curved plate of a star-enclosing shell. 64 of them close the sphere.$(br2)Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().
